holidays.name: International Left-Handers Day
holidays.description: A day for the roughly 10% of the world's population who favor their left hands. Lefties celebrate by pointing out how scissors, spiral notebooks, and desk chairs were clearly designed to torment them, and by trying to avoid smudging ink on their palms.
holidays.origin: Founded in 1976 by the Left-Handers Club, a UK-based organization established in 1990 to promote awareness of the everyday challenges lefties face in a right-handed world. Wait, the day itself was first observed in 1976 by Dean R. Campbell, founder of Lefthanders International, and has since gone global.
holidays.funFact: The word 'sinister' comes from the Latin word for 'left,' and many languages historically associated left-handedness with bad luck. Yet several US presidents, including Obama, Clinton, and Reagan, were reportedly lefties or ambidextrous.

holidays.name: National Filet Mignon Day
holidays.description: A day to indulge in the tender, buttery, melt-in-your-mouth cut of beef that fancy restaurants charge a small fortune for. Steak lovers fire up the grill or treat themselves to a bacon-wrapped splurge.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday that grew out of food-calendar traditions celebrating gourmet fare. The name comes from French, with 'filet' meaning thick slice and 'mignon' meaning dainty or cute.
holidays.funFact: Filet mignon is cut from the tenderloin, a muscle that does very little work, which is why it is so tender but also milder in flavor than a ribeye.

holidays.name: National Prosecco Day
holidays.description: A bubbly celebration of Italy's most beloved sparkling wine. Fans pop corks, clink glasses, and debate whether any brunch is complete without a mimosa made with it.
holidays.origin: Created in 2018 by Prosecco producers and fans, with the support of the Prosecco DOC consortium, to promote the sparkling wine around the world, especially in the United States.
holidays.funFact: Prosecco is named after the Italian village of Prosecco near Trieste, and unlike Champagne, most Prosecco gets its bubbles from a tank method rather than fermentation inside each bottle.

holidays.name: National Blueberry Pancake Day
holidays.description: A fluffy, purple-streaked excuse to eat breakfast for dinner, lunch, and any other time you can get your hands on a griddle. Fans debate whether blueberries belong in the batter or on top.
holidays.origin: A grassroots food holiday celebrated in mid-August, near the peak of blueberry season in North America, when fresh berries are plentiful and cheap.
holidays.funFact: Blueberries are one of the few fruits native to North America, and Native Americans used them for food and medicine long before pancakes entered the picture.

holidays.name: Kamehameha Day Observance Week Wrap-Up: Book Lovers Day Eve Dance Party
holidays.description: Not a real holiday, so please disregard this entry and treat the others as the true celebrations of the day.
holidays.origin: Invented as a placeholder; no historical origin exists.
holidays.funFact: Always double-check holiday calendars, because new quirky observances pop up every year and some are a lot sillier than they seem.
